segments.name: Flexible friends planning a cheap escape
Flexible couple seeking a cheap short break

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: The member fare of 528 HKD is within my 547 HKD budget and clearly below the 660 HKD normal fare, which suits a very price-sensitive bargain hunter. I am keen for an optional break after six months without leisure travel, and friends are flexible on dates and destination. Okinawa is only mildly appealing, but at this price it is a worthwhile cheap escape.

analysis.summary: Of 16 members, 4 bought at the 528 HKD member fare and 12 declined. Nine declines were inventory/budget-environment forced, not price objections. Three declines cited low trip interest or optional-leisure appeal rather than fare level. The current fare equals the permitted cap, so no higher test is allowed. Buyers cited the discount as compelling, but buying at today's fare does not prove willingness to pay more. Evidence is mixed and does not support a clear directional price test.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 528 HKD fare on fresh members will reproduce roughly 20-25% weighted conversion, with most declines driven by unavailable inventory or low optional-trip interest rather than fare level; a materially different conversion would contradict this.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: Most declines (10 of 13) cite no ticket both available and within basic-fare budget, an inventory/budget constraint rather than a stated price objection; two cite low destination appeal or free-time preference, and one is optional leisure. Three members bought at 496 HKD, each explicitly saying they would not pay the 660 HKD regular fare. No customer explicitly objects to the 496 fare as too high. Evidence is mixed: purchases show the member fare works, but declines are dominated by availability, not price.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a lower member fare on fresh customers will not meaningfully raise conversion, because most declines stem from unavailable inventory rather than fare level; conversion should stay within a few points of the current rate.

analysis.summary: At the current 288 HKD member fare, 10 of 16 customers bought and 6 declined. All six declines cite low trip interest and a strong preference to keep schedule and money, not the fare itself; one decline is environment-forced. Buyers repeatedly describe 288 as a compelling bargain below their budgets, and several would decline the 660 regular fare. No inventory denials occurred and quota is far from binding. Evidence points to price-sensitive optional-trip demand rather than a fare objection, so the direction is to test a higher fare on fresh customers.

analysis.summary: At the current 356 HKD member fare, 4 of 16 members bought, citing strong value versus the 660 HKD normal fare. Most declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), not price objections. Several declines were low-interest optional-leisure choices where price was explicitly affordable. No customer objected to the fare itself. Evidence supports testing the same fare on fresh customers rather than lowering or raising it, though the small sample and many inventory denials limit confidence.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 356 HKD member fare on fresh customers will yield a weighted conversion not materially below the observed 0.24, since declines stem mainly from inventory limits and low trip interest rather than fare objections.

analysis.summary: At the current 328 HKD member fare, 8 of 16 customers bought, citing the fare as a standout bargain versus the 660 HKD normal fare. Four declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), and four were low destination appeal or casual browsing, not price objections. No customer objected to the fare itself. The paired initial at 528 HKD converted far fewer buyers, suggesting the lower fare drives conversion, but this is untested for fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will reduce conversion enough that basic ticket receipts fall below those at the current 328 HKD fare, because buyers repeatedly cite the discount versus the 660 HKD normal fare as decisive.

analysis.summary: At the 303 HKD member fare, 11 of 15 customers bought and 4 declined. Most buyers cite the low fare as the decisive trigger, with several stating they would refuse the 660 HKD normal fare. Two declines are inventory/budget-forced, and two reflect low trip interest rather than price. The current fare sits well below the 528 HKD cap, and paired metrics show higher revenue at 303 than at 528. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying today does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts above the 303 HKD baseline, since most current buyers cite the fare as a bargain well under their stated ceilings.

assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
Base fares only; all taxes/fuel/add-ons and operating costs excluded. Revenue is not airline profit.
Population weights are explicit scenario assumptions, not measured HK Express market shares.
Fresh stratified members each search round; paired candidate and initial quote in reset, blinded worlds. One seat per member per world.
Only declared public segment/flexibility enter learning; private budgets, motivation and simulator constraints remain environment-only.
Every third round may test a cited LLM direction within a bounded model-scored interval; text never adds a demand label.
Analyst requests allow at most three attempts within the shared call budget. Unavailable analysis supplies no direction; recorded purchases still train Thompson and undergo independent confirmation.
Quoted fares are whole HKD; weighted averages and statistical estimates may have decimals.
Parallel intent elicitation followed by fixed-priority integer inventory clearing; no seat is reserved by an LLM.
Weighted demand estimates and actual panel cash/seat transactions are reported separately.
Final member quotes round down to an amount ending in nine, with any result below HK$30 becoming HK$0; raw search prices remain recorded.
Independent validation compares the formatted initial fallback, formatted selected fare and no offer after freezing both final quotes; no refitting on holdout.
